sender: Premier Valley Roofing (sales rep: R. Dale), Fairview Glen, CA
headline: This is a $20,250 roof replacement estimate with several warning signs.
summary: Premier Valley Roofing wants $20,250 to replace your 1,800 sq ft shingle roof. The price is higher than typical for this size of roof. The paper has no contractor license number, asks for a very large deposit, and pushes you to sign today. Do not sign or pay yet.

deadline.what_is_due: The estimate says the price is 'good today only,' but there is no real deadline. You do not have to decide today. The estimate is dated {{DATE:-1}}.

if_ignored: Nothing happens if you do not sign. This is an offer, not a bill. The price may change, but a fair contractor will give you time to compare quotes.

action_steps.title: Do not sign or pay today
action_steps.detail: A 'good today only' price is a pressure tactic. Tell the salesperson you need a few days to compare quotes.

action_steps.title: Check the contractor's license
action_steps.detail: No license number is on this estimate. Ask for it in writing, then look it up on the California Contractors State License Board site. Make sure it is active and matches the business name.

action_steps.title: Get 2–3 other written quotes
action_steps.detail: Ask each roofer to price the same work: 18 squares of shingles, underlayment, flashing, and tear-off. Compare line by line.

action_steps.title: Ask for a smaller deposit
action_steps.detail: In California, a deposit on home work cannot be more than 10% of the price or $1,000, whichever is less. The $8,100 deposit is much higher. Do not pay it.

action_steps.title: Ask for a detailed written contract
action_steps.detail: It should explain 'misc materials' and 'labor,' name the shingle brand and warranty, give start and finish dates, and say who pulls the city permit.

action_steps.title: Avoid paying cash
action_steps.detail: The 5% cash discount leaves you no payment record. Pay by check or card so you can prove what you paid.

red_flags.text: No California contractor license number appears anywhere. A roofing job this size must be done by a licensed contractor.
The deposit is 40% ($8,100). California law caps it at 10% or $1,000, whichever is less.
'Special price good today only' and 'price goes up if not signed today' are high-pressure sales tactics.
'Misc materials' ($2,400) is vague and has no details.
'Labor' is only $1,750 with no hours or crew size. This looks low for a full re-roof.
A 5% discount for cash payment can mean no paper trail.
The start date is 'to be scheduled,' with no finish date, no written warranty, and no mention of permits.
The tear-off ($3,200) and underlayment ($1,800) prices are on the high side.

reasons: No contractor license number is shown.
Pressure to sign today and a large deposit are common in roofing scams.
Vague items and no start or finish dates leave you with little protection.
Verify the business's license and address yourself before paying anything.

line_items.item: Tear-off existing shingles (1 layer) & haul away debris
Flashing, drip edge, pipe boots & ridge vents

line_items.typical_range: No hours given; installed prices usually already include labor (estimate)

questions_to_ask: What is your California contractor license number, and can I see proof of insurance and workers' compensation?
What exactly is in 'misc materials' and what does 'labor' cover, with hours and crew size?
Can the deposit be lowered to $1,000 or 10% (whichever is less), with the rest paid in steps as work is finished?
What are the start and finish dates, shingle brand, and written warranty? Who gets the city permit?
